original.target_description: Manuscript p. 8 Code snippets paragraph: omnibus ANOVA comparing mean comprehension/answer accuracy Acc across S1–S5.

n.sample_role: Snippet-level subject responses/observations across five snippets from 104 distinct participants; repeated observations, not 520 independent participants.
n.exclusions: 255 started; 110 completed; six completers excluded for extremely short code-reading and question-answering times. Final 104 participants supplied 520 observations. Three participants declaring a reading disorder were retained because their data were not outliers. No additional target-specific exclusions reported.
n.location: Manuscript p. 6 §6; p. 7 Table 3 ALL row and §7.
n.quote: The remaining 104 subjects provided ... 520 datapoints in total; 104 per snippet and between 14 and ... only included the data from those 104 subjects.

es.location: Manuscript p. 8 §7 Code snippets; p. 7 Table 3.
es.quote: significant differences in the overall perceived readability ... (R1) (χ2 = 22.8; α = 0.004) as well as in their mean answer ... accuracy (Acc) (ANOVA p = 0.0013 at α < 0.01)

notes: Identity verified from canonical text: accepted peer-reviewed primary experimental report, matching title The Role of Method Chains and Comments in Software Readability and Comprehension – An Experiment, authors Jürgen Börstler and Barbara Paech, DOI 10.1109/TSE.2016.2527791. Full methods/results/appendices, manuscript pp. 1–17 after repository cover. Final journal pagination differs. No PDF supplied; no rendering. Only unfinished fields examined; other fields/sides are placeholders. The p. 8 locator and explicit S1–S5 mean-answer-accuracy paragraph identify the comprehension comparison. ANOVA p = 0.0013 is printed but no F statistic or named omnibus effect size. χ2 = 22.8 in that paragraph concerns readability R1 and is not assigned to comprehension. Table 3 provides descriptive Acc means only. N = 520 directly printed observations, with 104 contributors; no sum or df inference. Unassigned p remains a placeholder.
